newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50--dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50--dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices were steady to $0.50 lower early, weakened by sluggish demand, livestock dealers said.
Soft pork prices weighed on the market although fairly light receipts helped to limit early losses. USDA pork cut-out values were off $0.20 to $0.28 Friday.

In Iowa-southern Minnesota there was early trade for plants at $56.50 per cwt with a few as high as $57.00, while in the country the early top was around $56.00, representing an overall trend of steady to $0.50 lower.
In Illinois prices were seen steady to off $0.50 per cwt with early buying interest reported to be "slow".
One Illinois dealer said a light run should help to underpin prices.
The run was also light further east in the Indiana, Ohio area where prices were expected to be about steady.
